children: By Pawel Florkiewicz and Karol Badohal

The National Bank of Poland held its main interest rate at 3.75% on Wednesday, saying it expected inflation to remain within its target range for the rest of this year, although its prospects are uncertain.

The NBP said it sees inflation of 3.1%-3.2% in 2026, which would be within its inflation target of 1.5% to 3.5%. Then the price growth rate will accelerate to between 3.1% and 5.3% in 2027 before slowing to a range of 1.4% to 4.4% in 2028.
Preliminary October data published last Friday showed annual inflation slowed more than expected to 3.5% and the central bank said core inflation also eased last month.
"Further decisions of the Council will depend on incoming information regarding prospects for inflation and economic activity in Poland," the Monetary Policy Council said in a statement.
"Particularly important is macroeconomic situation abroad, including developments in global commodity prices and inflation, amid changing geopolitical context."
The MPC decision was in line with the expectations of a majority of analysts surveyed by Reuters - 26 out of 29 - while the remaining three had expected the rate to rise to 4.00%.
TIGHTENING MAY COME NEXT YEAR, SOME ANALYSTS SAY

With such forecasts, the NBP could raise rates, but it wants to wait and see if the government decides to extend measures protecting households against rising energy and fuel prices, analysts at Bank Pekao SA said.
"Paraphrasing, it won't fire until it sees the whites of their eyes," Pekao wrote in a comment.
Analysts predict that a tightening of monetary policy could come next year.

"This inflation projection supports our scenario, which assumes 50-basis-point hikes in early 2027 — though the outcome depends on the durability of the correction in the commodities market," said ING analysts.

The central bank will publish details of the new projection this week, and investors are now awaiting Thursday's press conference by central bank governor Adam Glapinski, who will explain the MPC's November decision.
At its previous policy meeting in early October, the NBP also left interest rates unchanged >. At that time, Glapinski said that, while options were open, he did not expect a November hike.
